subject: Post-demo: rate capacity, overage pathways & pricing checklist
thread_text:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-22 09:14 PDT
Subject: Post-demo: rate capacity, overage pathways & pricing checklist

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for jumping on the call this morning. Quick recap and the few items we agreed to follow up on:

1) Workload profile (what we saw today)
   - 95th percentile request size: ~1.8k tokens (prompt + response).
   - Average daily token volume: ~35M tokens, peak minute spikes up to ~2.5M tokens (short windows).

2) Budget target and unit economics
   - You mentioned a target spend of $8k–$12k / month for this phase.
   - Target unit: ideally <= $800 / 1M tokens for inference (we discussed tradeoffs between latency and quantization).

3) Rate limits & burst behavior
   - You need soft burst capacity for short spikes (up to ~3x baseline for 2–5 minute windows).
   - Want predictable overage terms rather than surprise throttling.

Action items I promised:
   A) Concrete pricing options: baseline per-1M tier + burst windows and overage rates (see attached PDF).
   B) A brief capacity proposal with concrete quotas / soft caps and a one-page summary of fallback behavior (what happens when soft cap is hit).
   C) Example cost scenarios using your spreadsheet — I attached a filled-in worksheet for the volumes we discussed.

Next steps / asks from you:
   - Confirm whether the 2–5 minute spike window is accurate for worst-case events.
   - Confirm whether you prefer overage billed monthly vs. prefunded credit applied to burst usage.

I looped in Ben (pricing lead) and Karthik (solutions) to propose 2 pricing paths we can operationalize quickly.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachment: Redwood-Rate-Limits-Pricing-Options.pdf (summary + rate table)

From: Samir Rao <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22 11:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: rate capacity, overage pathways & pricing checklist

Hannah —

Thanks for the recap, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Spike window: 3–6 minutes for the absolute worst-case (we have a nightly batch plus interactive queries). Spikes come from concurrent user sessions, not long-running single requests. 2–5 minutes is fair for typical peaks, but plan for 6 mins as a safety buffer.
- Budget: the $8k–$12k is our initial pilot spending envelope; if the per-1M math swings above ~$950 we’d likely need an exec sign-off.
- Prefund vs monthly overage: we prefer prefunded/bucketed credit for burst — simplifies procurement and caps surprises.

Two asks: 1) can you show an option where we pre-buy a burst credit pool (e.g., 10M tokens) that only applies to minute-level spikes (not normal usage)? 2) what are the SLA/latency differences between the baseline model and the quantized low-cost variant?

—Samir
CTO, FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com
+1 (212) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23 08:46 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: rate capacity, overage pathways & pricing checklist

Samir / Hannah —

Thanks for the detail — I put together two clear pathways below. Numbers are illustrative but aligned with the volumes you shared. See the attached PDF for a clean table.

Option A — Predictable baseline + small burst credit (recommended for pilots)
  - Baseline commit: 30M tokens / month at $850 / 1M = $25,500/mo (discounted baseline rate).
  - Burst credit bucket: pre-purchase 10M tokens at $700 / 1M usable only for minute-level spikes (automatic drawdown).
  - When bucket exhausted: soft-throttle to baseline model but allow queued requests for up to 60s; overage rate (if you opt-in) = $1,200 / 1M.
  - Rationale: caps month-to-month volatility, keeps effective unit cost near your target for pilot.

Option B — Lower commit + on-demand burst (lower upfront cost)
  - Baseline commit: 15M tokens / month at $950 / 1M = $14,250/mo.
  - No pre-purchase burst bucket; allow up to 3x short bursts for 3 minutes with a per-burst surcharge: $0.002/token during burst windows (equivalent to $2,000 / 1M only for burst tokens).
  - If you hit sustained >3x for more than 10 minutes, we initiate rate-based fallback to a cheaper quantized model to preserve availability.
  - Rationale: lower initial spend, but higher marginal for bursts — good if spikes are rare.

Operational notes (both options):
  - Burst definition: token throughput above 200% of baseline minute-level throughput for >30s.
  - We expose a soft-cap and an alerting webhook so you can pre-emptively top up the burst bucket.
  - Billing: we can invoice monthly or convert burst bucket to a prepaid credit on PO.
  - SLA: baseline model (non-quantized) maintained at our 99.5% token-generation availability; quantized variant trades some latency/consistency for lower cost — typical latency delta 20–35% and occasional ~2–3% variance in sample fidelity on hallucination-sensitive prompts.

If this looks reasonable I can turn these into a one-page commercial summary + sample invoice for procurement.

—Ben
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir@finlytics.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-23 10:12 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-demo: rate capacity, overage pathways & pricing checklist

Samir —

Quick note on the operational behavior if you pick Option A (burst bucket):
- Token accounting: burst tokens are charged from the pre-bought pool before baseline tokens. We tag burst traffic by request header and minute-window.
- Rollover: unused burst tokens do NOT roll over month-to-month for pilots; for annual contracts we can negotiate partial rollover.
- Monitoring: we’ll provide a per-minute telemetry endpoint and a Slack webhook for threshold alerts (we recommend 80% bucket threshold alert).

Also, for the quantized variant: we can run a 48-hour A/B with a sample of your production traffic (on a staging token) so you can see real delta in cost and QA metrics.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks everyone — Option A looks like the right balance for our pilot. Two final asks before procurement: 1) please produce the one-page commercial summary + sample PO with the prepaid burst bucket flow, and 2) add a short note in the SOW that the 10M burst bucket is only applied to minute-level spikes and excludes routine batch jobs.

If you can get that to us by EOD Friday we’ll schedule procurement review for next Tuesday.

—Samir
